[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is the 2-furoyl piperazine quinazoline (prazosin), structurally closest to terazosin and doxazosin; L4 reported terazosin as almost completely absorbed in humans (C135), doxazosin as completely absorbed (C161), and UK-294,315 as completely absorbed in dog and at least 86% absorbed in humans (C147, C174).

L5 Caco-2 records for related piperazine/heteroaromatic scaffolds show high absorptive permeability and low efflux ratios: IS0042 Papp A-B ~56-62 x10^-6 cm/s with ER ~1.0 (C213, C201, C181); compound 14 Papp 102 nm/s with ER 1.0 (C194, C197); compound 20 Papp 190 nm/s with ER 0.5 (C188, C207); BAY-885 Papp A-B 184 nm/s with ER 0.6 (C175, C212, C222); compound 49 Papp 175 nm/s with ER 0.42 (C199); and a 4-methylpiperazine moiety increased Papp_AB and decreased efflux (C206).

L6 provides no query-specific hepatic clearance measurement; the closest analog terazosin shows moderate hepatic/microsomal clearance in rats (non-renal CL 19.8 mL/min/kg, C259; CLint 0.0142 mL/min/mg, C240/C239) and CYP3A-mediated metabolism (C235/C271), while doxazosin shows moderate-to-high hepatocyte turnover (C227) but is completely absorbed (C161). These records do not establish an F < 20% first-pass barrier.

Direct oral bioavailability values for related N-acylpiperazine or dimethoxy-substituted scaffolds are all at or above the F >= 20% threshold: delavirdine 85% (C16), suvorexant 82% (C23), GSK1322322 57% fasted (C29), valbenazine ~49% (C03), brigatinib 46% (C28), donepezil ~100% (C04, C06), piritrexim ~75% with patient values 40-63% (C14, C22), and metoclopramide 79-82% (C15, C18).

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability or matched oral/IV exposure record exists for the query molecule itself; support is from close analogs (terazosin, doxazosin) and related scaffolds.

No query-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic stability measurement is supplied; L6 records are analog-based and include some high-clearance compounds (e.g., UK-294,315 HLM t1/2 6 min, C238/C249) that are not transferred to the query.
Furan and aniline moieties are potential metabolic liabilities, but no query-specific first-pass quantification is available.
Some L5 P-gp substrate records (UK-294,315, tandutinib) are not query-specific; UK-294,315 had high absorption despite efflux.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high: F >= 20% remains well supported. L6 adds mechanistic hepatic-clearance evidence for close analogs showing moderate, not overwhelming, first-pass metabolism (terazosin C259/C240; doxazosin C227 with complete absorption C161), and no query-specific record indicates F < 20%. Combined with high absorption/permeability evidence for the quinazoline-piperazine class and direct F values >=46% for related scaffolds, the high prediction is strengthened.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
